title: Data Handling: Tally Marks, Pictographs and Tables
seo_title: Tally Marks, Pictographs and Tables Class 2 Worksheet with Answers (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 11)
standard_code: Class 2, Joyful Mathematics Chapter 11: Data Handling
standard_text: Data handling: collecting data, recording with tally marks, and reading and drawing simple pictographs and tables (summary of NCERT Joyful Mathematics Class 2)
meta_desc: Class 2 Data Handling worksheet (Joyful Mathematics Chapter 11): tally marks, pictographs with a key, tables, most and fewest, totals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Use the key: one picture may stand for 2 or more.
key_sub: Tally marks are grouped in fives.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Tally marks: |||| with a line across = 5.
  • In a pictograph, read the key: if one picture = 2, then 4 pictures = 8.

Examples

Example

Key: one star = 2 children. Mangoes has 5 stars.

5 × 2

Answer: 10 children

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting pictures without using the keyMultiply by what each picture stands for.
Reading the wrong rowPut your finger on the row's name first.

faq.a: A chart that uses pictures to show data, with a key saying how much each picture stands for.
Marks drawn in groups of five to count.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5. Count in 5s: 5. So it is 5.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 1 group of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7. So it is 7.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10. So it is 10.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: What number does this tally show?
items.e: Four lines with one line across make a group of 5. 3 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17, 18. So it is 18.

items.q: How many children chose strawberry?
items.e: Find the Strawberry row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12. So it is 12.

items.q: How many children chose grapes?
items.e: Find the Grapes row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13.

items.q: How many pigeons were seen?
items.e: Find the Pigeon row. It has 2 groups of 5 and 1 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11. So it is 11.

items.q: How many children come by car?
items.e: Find the Car row. It has 1 group of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7. So it is 7.

items.q: Which row shows 14 children?
items.e: 14 is 5 + 5 + 4. The Skipping row has 2 groups of 5 and 4 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13, 14. So it is 14.

items.q: Which row shows 8 cars?
items.e: 8 is 5 + 3. The White row has 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8.

items.q: Which fruit is the most popular?
items.e: Count every row: Grapes 13, Banana 18, Orange 10, Apple 4. The biggest number is 18, for Banana.

items.q: Which way do the fewest children come to school?
items.e: Count every row: Scooter 5, Car 7, Bike 13, Walk 8. The smallest number is 5, for Scooter.

items.q: Which tally shows 8?
items.e: C is right: 1 group of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, then 6, 7, 8. So it is 8. A: it has one mark too many; B: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; D: it has one mark too few.

items.q: Which tally shows 13?
items.e: A is right: 2 groups of 5 and 3 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13. So it is 13. B: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s; C: it has one mark too few; D: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6.

items.q: Which tally shows 17?
items.e: D is right: 3 groups of 5 and 2 more. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, then 16, 17. So it is 17. A: the groups have five upright lines and a line across, so each group is 6; B: it has one mark too many; C: the groups have no line across, so they are hard to count in 5s.

items.q: How many more children chose chocolate than vanilla?
items.e: Chocolate: 17. Vanilla: 2. How many more means find the difference: 17 − 2 = 15.

items.q: How many fewer robins than sparrows were seen?
items.e: Sparrow: 15. Robin: 6. How many fewer means find the difference: 15 − 6 = 9.

items.q: How many children voted altogether?
items.e: Count every row: Hopscotch 9, Football 5, Skipping 14, Tag 12. Then add: 9 + 5 + 14 + 12 = 40.

items.q: How many cars went past altogether?
items.e: Count every row: White 8, Red 14, Silver 15, Black 13. Then add: 8 + 14 + 15 + 13 = 50.

items.q: How many worms were found?
items.e: Each circle = 1 small creature. Count the circles in the Worm row: 1 worm.
Each star = 1 child. Count the stars in the Strawberry row: 7 children.

items.q: How many children have a hamster?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Count the squares in the Hamster row: 5 children.
Each heart = 1 child. Count the hearts in the Orange row: 3 children.

items.q: How many silver cars went past?
items.e: Each circle = 1 car. Count the circles in the Silver row: 6 cars.
Each star = 1 child. Count the stars in the Tag row: 4 children.

items.q: Which row shows 8 children?
items.e: Each square = 1 child. Look for the row with 8 squares. That is Purple.
Each heart = 1 bird. Look for the row with 9 hearts. That is Blackbird.

items.q: Which way do the most children come to school?
items.e: Each circle = 1 child. The Car row has the most circles: 9.
Each star = 1 child. The Chocolate row has the most stars: 8.

items.q: How many students come to school by MRT?
items.e: The MRT row has 6 pictures. Each picture stands for 1. So the answer is 6 students. (9 is the Bus row.)

items.q: How many students come to school by bus?
items.e: The Bus row has 9 pictures. Each picture stands for 1. So the answer is 9 students. (4 is the Car row.)

items.q: How many students walk to school?
items.e: The Walk row has 3 pictures. Each picture stands for 1. So the answer is 3 students. (4 is the Car row.)

items.q: Which row shows 4 students?
items.e: Each picture stands for 1. Car has 4 pictures. Count the pictures: 1, 2, 3, 4. So Car shows 4.

items.q: Which way to school is the most popular?
items.e: The longest row has the most pictures. Bus has 9 pictures, which is 9 students. All the pictures stand for the same number, so you can compare the rows.
The Pooja row has 5 pictures. Each picture stands for 1. So the answer is 5 stickers. (8 is the Harsh row.)
The Harsh row has 8 pictures. Each picture stands for 1. So the answer is 8 stickers. (6 is the Priya row.)
The Rehan row has 3 pictures. Each picture stands for 1. So the answer is 3 stickers. (6 is the Priya row.)
Each picture stands for 1. Priya has 6 pictures. Count the pictures: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. So Priya shows 6.
Look at the key under the graph: each picture stands for 1 sticker. Always read the key before you count.

items.q: How many children chose purple?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 children, so half a circle = 1. The Purple row has 7 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So it is 14 children.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Chocolate row has 6 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: How many children chose tag?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Tag row has 3 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20, 30. So it is 30 children.

items.q: How many blue tits were seen?
items.e: Look at the key: each circle = 2 birds, so half a circle = 1. The Blue tit row has 2 circles. Count in 2s: 2, 4. So it is 4 blue tits.
Look at the key: each star = 2 small creatures, so half a star = 1. The Worm row has 3 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, then 1 more for the half. So it is 7 worms.
Look at the key: each star = 5 children. The Bus row has 7 stars. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So it is 35 children.

items.q: How many children chose apples?
items.e: Look at the key: each square = 10 children. The Apple row has 2 squares. Count in 10s: 10, 20. So it is 20 children.
Look at the key: each star = 2 children, so half a star = 1. The Dog row has 3 stars and half a star. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, then 1 more for the half. So it is 7 children.

items.q: Each square stands for 5 children. 20 children chose tag. How many squares go in the Tag row?
items.e: Count in 5s until you reach 20: 5, 10, 15, 20. That is 4 steps, so draw 4 squares, not 20.

items.q: Each circle stands for 10 children. 60 children walk to school. How many circles go in the Walk row?
items.e: Count in 10s until you reach 60: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. That is 6 steps, so draw 6 circles, not 60.

items.q: What does each picture stand for?
items.e: Look at the key under the graph: each picture stands for 2 students. Always read the key before you count.

items.q: How many students chose football?
items.e: The Football row has 7 pictures. Each picture stands for 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So the answer is 14 students. Do not just count the pictures: 7 pictures are not 7 students.

items.q: How many students chose choir?
items.e: The Choir row has 5 pictures. Each picture stands for 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. So the answer is 10 students. Do not just count the pictures: 5 pictures are not 5 students.

items.q: How many students chose art club?
items.e: The Art club row has 8 pictures. Each picture stands for 2. Count in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. So the answer is 16 students. Do not just count the pictures: 8 pictures are not 8 students.

items.q: 12 students chose basketball. How many pictures are needed for basketball?
items.e: Each picture stands for 2. Count in 2s until you reach 12: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. That is 6 pictures.
Look at the key under the graph: each picture stands for 5 stickers. Always read the key before you count.
The Gauri row has 6 pictures. Each picture stands for 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So the answer is 30 stickers. Do not just count the pictures: 6 pictures are not 6 stickers.
The Kavya row has 7 pictures. Each picture stands for 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. So the answer is 35 stickers. Do not just count the pictures: 7 pictures are not 7 stickers.
The Nikhil row has 3 pictures. Each picture stands for 5. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15. So the answer is 15 stickers. Do not just count the pictures: 3 pictures are not 3 stickers.
Each picture stands for 5. Dev has 4 pictures. Count in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20. So Dev shows 20.

items.q: How many children chose purple?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Count the blocks in the Purple column: 7. The top of the column is at 7 on the scale.

items.q: How many days were sunny?
items.e: Each block = 1 day. Count the blocks in the Sunny column: 11. The top of the column is at 11 on the scale.

items.q: How many woodlice were found?
items.e: Each block = 1 small creature. Count the blocks in the Woodlouse column: 3. The top of the column is at 3 on the scale.

items.q: Which column shows 9 children?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The Rabbit column has 9 blocks.

items.q: Which game is the most popular?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The tallest column is Football: 12.

items.q: Which way do the fewest children come to school?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. The shortest column is Bike: 2.

items.q: How many more children chose strawberry than chocolate?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Strawberry: 10. Chocolate: 3. How many more means find the difference: 10 − 3 = 7.

items.q: How many fewer children chose grapes than oranges?
items.e: Each block = 1 child. Orange: 7. Grapes: 3. How many fewer means find the difference: 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: Put the colours in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Black 4, White 7, Silver 12, Blue 11. Biggest first: Silver (12), Blue (11), White (7), Black (4).

items.q: Put the birds in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Sparrow 9, Blue tit 8, Robin 3, Pigeon 10. Smallest first: Robin (3), Blue tit (8), Sparrow (9), Pigeon (10).

items.q: How many silver cars went past?
items.e: Find the Silver row, then read the number next to it: 3 cars.

items.q: How many children come by bus?
items.e: Find the Bus row, then read the number next to it: 6 children.

items.q: Which pet do the most children have?
items.e: Read the table. The biggest number is Dog: 17.

items.q: Put the games in order from most to fewest.
items.e: Read each one: Hopscotch 14, Football 19, Skipping 17, Tag 18. Biggest first: Football (19), Tag (18), Skipping (17), Hopscotch (14).

items.q: How many small creatures were found altogether?
items.e: Read the table. Add all the numbers: 12 + 3 + 19 + 16 = 50.

items.q: How many more children chose green than red?
items.e: Read the table. Green: 17. Red: 14. How many more means find the difference: 17 − 14 = 3.

items.q: How many children from Class 2B go to Choir?
items.e: Find the Choir row, then go across to the Class 2B column: 13. (6 is the Class 2A column.)

items.q: How many children go to Football altogether?
items.e: Football row: Class 2A 9, Class 2B 12. Altogether means add: 9 + 12 = 21.

items.q: Which fruit is the least popular?
items.e: Read the table. The smallest number is Pear: 3.

items.q: Put the flavours in order from fewest to most.
items.e: Read each one: Vanilla 2, Strawberry 9, Mint 18, Chocolate 10. Smallest first: Vanilla (2), Strawberry (9), Chocolate (10), Mint (18).

items.q: Which food is the most popular?
items.e: The longest row has the most pictures. Pulao has 8 pictures, which is 40 students. All the pictures stand for the same number, so you can compare the rows.

items.q: Which food is the least popular?
items.e: The shortest row has the fewest pictures. Laksa has 4 pictures, which is 20 students. All the pictures stand for the same number, so you can compare the rows.

items.q: How many more students chose pulao than laksa?
items.e: Pulao: 40 students. Laksa: 20 students. Subtract: 40 − 20 = 20. Or: Pulao has 4 pictures more, and 4 × 5 = 20. Do not stop at 4.

items.q: How many more students chose satay than fish soup?
items.e: Satay: 30 students. Fish soup: 25 students. Subtract: 30 − 25 = 5. Or: Satay has 1 picture more, and 1 × 5 = 5. Do not stop at 1.

items.q: How many fewer students chose satay than pulao?
items.e: Pulao: 40 students. Satay: 30 students. Subtract: 40 − 30 = 10. Or: Pulao has 2 pictures more, and 2 × 5 = 10. Do not stop at 2.

items.q: On which day were the most durians sold?
items.e: The longest row has the most pictures. Saturday has 9 pictures, which is 90 durians. All the pictures stand for the same number, so you can compare the rows.

items.q: On which day were the fewest durians sold?
items.e: The shortest row has the fewest pictures. Monday has 3 pictures, which is 30 durians. All the pictures stand for the same number, so you can compare the rows.

items.q: How many more durians were sold on Saturday than on Friday?
items.e: Saturday: 90 durians. Friday: 60 durians. Subtract: 90 − 60 = 30. Or: Saturday has 3 pictures more, and 3 × 10 = 30. Do not stop at 3.

items.q: How many more durians were sold on Sunday than on Monday?
items.e: Sunday: 80 durians. Monday: 30 durians. Subtract: 80 − 30 = 50. Or: Sunday has 5 pictures more, and 5 × 10 = 50. Do not stop at 5.

items.q: How many fewer durians were sold on Monday than on Saturday?
items.e: Saturday: 90 durians. Monday: 30 durians. Subtract: 90 − 30 = 60. Or: Saturday has 6 pictures more, and 6 × 10 = 60. Do not stop at 6.

items.q: How many students chose red or blue?
items.e: Red: 12. Blue: 16. Add: 12 + 16 = 28. Or count all 14 pictures in 2s.

items.q: How many students chose yellow or green?
items.e: Yellow: 6. Green: 10. Add: 6 + 10 = 16. Or count all 8 pictures in 2s.

items.q: How many students chose a colour altogether?
items.e: Add all the rows: 12 + 16 + 6 + 10 = 44. Or: there are 22 pictures, and each stands for 2. 22 pictures is not 22.

items.q: How many students did not choose blue?
items.e: Add the other rows: 12 + 6 + 10 = 28. Or take away from the total: 44 − 16 = 28.

items.q: Which two colours were chosen by 26 students altogether?
items.e: Blue: 16. Green: 10. 16 + 10 = 26. Red and blue make 28, and red and green make 22, and so do blue and yellow.

items.q: How many shells did Shreya and Imran find altogether?
items.e: Shreya: 35. Imran: 20. Add: 35 + 20 = 55. Or count all 11 pictures in 5s.

items.q: How many shells did Pooja and Kumar find altogether?
items.e: Pooja: 30. Kumar: 15. Add: 30 + 15 = 45. Or count all 9 pictures in 5s.

items.q: How many shells did they find altogether?
items.e: Add all the rows: 35 + 20 + 30 + 15 = 100. Or: there are 20 pictures, and each stands for 5. 20 pictures is not 20.

items.q: Who found more shells: Shreya, or Imran and Kumar together?
items.e: Shreya found 35 shells. Imran and Kumar found 20 + 15 = 35 shells. 35 = 35, so they found the same. Imran and Kumar have 7 pictures together, the same as Shreya.

items.q: How many shells did the other three children find, not counting Pooja?
items.e: Add the other rows: 35 + 20 + 15 = 70. Or take away from the total: 100 − 30 = 70.
